data.q: What is the primary purpose of Clippy in the Rust ecosystem?
o: Static analysis and linting to catch common mistakes and improve code quality
data.e: Clippy is a collection of lints to catch common mistakes and improve your Rust code. It performs static analysis, while rustfmt handles formatting.

data.q: What is the primary purpose of rustfmt?
o: Code formatting according to community style guidelines
data.e: rustfmt automatically formats Rust code according to the standard style guide. It ensures consistent formatting across a codebase.

data.q: How do you install Clippy and rustfmt using rustup?
o: They are installed by default with the stable toolchain
data.e: Clippy and rustfmt are optional components installed via `rustup component add clippy rustfmt`. They are not installed by default with the minimal toolchain.

data.q: Which command runs Clippy lints on a Cargo project?
data.e: `cargo clippy` runs Clippy lints on the current Cargo package. It accepts the same arguments as `cargo check`.

data.q: Which command formats a Cargo project using rustfmt?
data.e: `cargo fmt` is the Cargo subcommand provided by rustfmt to format all crates in the workspace. `rustfmt` can also be run directly on files.

data.q: How can you allow a specific Clippy lint (e.g., `needless_lifetimes`) for an entire crate?
o: It is not possible to allow a lint crate-wide
data.e: Crate-level lint attributes like `#![allow(clippy::needless_lifetimes)]` are placed in the crate root (usually `lib.rs` or `main.rs`).

data.q: What does the `rustfmt.toml` or `.rustfmt.toml` file control?
o: Configuration options for rustfmt, such as max line width and indentation style
Editor integration settings for VS Code
data.e: rustfmt reads configuration from `rustfmt.toml` (or `.rustfmt.toml`) to customize formatting rules like `max_width`, `indent_style`, `use_small_heuristics`, etc.

data.q: Which Clippy lint group is enabled by default and includes lints for correctness, style, and complexity?
data.e: The `clippy::correctness` group (often referred to as the default set) is enabled by default when running `cargo clippy`. It catches actual bugs or suspicious code. `clippy::style` and `clippy::complexity` are also enabled by default in practice, but the group name is not 'standard'.

data.q: How do you run rustfmt in 'check' mode to verify formatting without modifying files (useful for CI)?
o: Both A and C are correct
data.e: Both `cargo fmt --check` and `rustfmt --check` will exit with a non-zero status if formatting changes are needed, without writing them. This is standard for CI pipelines.

data.q: What is the effect of the Clippy lint `clippy::unwrap_used`?
o: It warns when `unwrap()` is called on `Option` or `Result`, suggesting explicit error handling
It suggests using `unwrap()` for cleaner code
It is part of the default lint set
data.e: `clippy::unwrap_used` (from the `clippy::pedantic` group) warns against using `unwrap()` because it can panic. It encourages proper error handling with `?`, `match`, or `expect()` with a message.

data.q: Which command updates rustfmt to the latest version available in the current toolchain?
data.e: `rustup update` updates the entire toolchain, including the installed components like rustfmt and clippy. You don't update them individually via cargo.

data.q: How can you temporarily disable a Clippy lint for a specific function or block?
o: It is not possible to disable locally
data.e: Rust's lint attributes work on any item or statement. `#[allow(clippy::lint_name)]` placed directly above a function, block, or statement suppresses the lint for that scope.

data.q: What does the `clippy::pedantic` lint group contain?
o: Only lints that are guaranteed to be correct and never produce false positives
Lints that are strict, opinionated, or may have false positives; off by default
Lints that are deprecated and scheduled for removal
data.e: The `pedantic` group contains lints that are very strict or opinionated (e.g., `unwrap_used`, `missing_docs_in_private_items`). They are not enabled by default because they may be noisy or have false positives. Enable with `#![warn(clippy::pedantic)]` or `cargo clippy -W clippy::pedantic`.

data.q: Which file does rustfmt ignore by default when formatting a project?
o: Files listed in `.rustfmtignore` (or `.gitignore` if no `.rustfmtignore` exists)
data.e: rustfmt respects `.rustfmtignore` files with the same syntax as `.gitignore`. If `.rustfmtignore` doesn't exist, it falls back to `.gitignore`. It always skips the `target/` directory.

data.q: What is the recommended way to enforce formatting and linting in a CI pipeline?
o: Run `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy` and fail if they produce any output
Run `rustfmt --check` and `clippy -D warnings` directly on source files
Run `cargo test` which includes formatting and linting checks
data.e: `cargo fmt --check` fails if formatting is needed. `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` treats all lints (including Clippy's) as errors, causing a non-zero exit code. This is the standard CI pattern.

data.q: How do you configure Clippy lints per-project in `Cargo.toml`?
o: Clippy cannot be configured in Cargo.toml
data.e: Since Cargo 1.80 (stabilized in 1.81), you can configure lints (including Clippy's) in `Cargo.toml` under `[workspace.lints]` or `[package.lints]` tables, e.g., `clippy::unwrap_used = "deny"`.
